# Getting Started

**Source:** https://open.seatalk.io/docs/Getting-Started

This page covers the steps to create a simple SeaTalk Bot, set up event callbacks, subscribe to the bot (deprecate now), etc. The Bot will be capable of sending and receiving messages, in private chat.

- Register New Bot

- Receive Interaction

- Initiate Action

Before starting, we recommend you to download the example code (https://cdnid.sp-cdn.susercontent.com/api/v4/50093511/slimud/b703e2b2e4b3ef55d7761a6dd9e202e3/getting-started-bot.zip) that will be used throughout this tutorial.

## 1. Register New Bot 

From open.seatalk.io (https://open.seatalk.io/), click on "Start building" or "Create app" to trigger the app creation wizard. You can also trigger this by clicking "Create app" from you app list. Follow the steps in the wizard to complete the basic configuration of your app.

Step 1: Basic app information

![](https://sos.sp-cdn.shopee.com/c3/53693910/sos/A3oxOOqFANg1dBBkEdMDACc?sign=1756710638.2870235-M6LUz-0-f107eb5ba495a8fa82fd665b8deb14dd)

Step 2: Service and data scope configuration

![](https://sos.sp-cdn.shopee.com/c3/53693910/sos/A3oxOGCAACTIdRBkETMAACc?sign=1756710663.6995506-cNkDV-0-25b73208b00f815a4c6032041b8242a0)

Your new app will have a default status of Not Configured. Learn more about app statuses. (https://open.seatalk.io/docs/SOP-App-Statuses) Click the Enable button in the Bot card in the Capability section.

![](https://sos.sp-cdn.shopee.com/c3/53693910/sos/A3oxOI0mADSpeRBkEcoCACc?sign=1756710727.3357124-PnVvx-0-913a4a355acc95850c2310d7f85c309d)

Once a capability is successfully enabled, it will appear in the menu on the left hand side of the page, and you will be directed to the capability configuration menu of the newly added capability. Additionally, default API permissions for the capability will be enabled for your app.

2. Receive Interaction

### 2.1 Prepare Bot API Callback

To enable SOP to call to our service, whether it's to authenticate our Bot or receiving events, our Bot need to provide one API. Let's first create an API with an URI "/callback".

```
package main

import (
	"context"
	"log"
	"net/http"
	"os"
	"os/signal"
	"syscall"
	"time"

	"github.com/gin-gonic/gin"
)

func main() {
	c := make(chan os.Signal)
	signal.Notify(c, os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM, syscall.SIGHUP, syscall.SIGINT, syscall.SIGKILL, syscall.SIGQUIT)
	r := gin.Default()

	r.POST("/callback", func(ctx *gin.Context) {
		ctx.JSON(http.StatusOK, gin.H{
			"message": "Callback API",
		})
	})

	srv := &http.Server{
		Addr: ":8080",
		Handler: r,
	}

	go func() {
		log.Println("starting web, listening on", srv.Addr)
		err := srv.ListenAndServe()
		if err != nil && err != http.ErrServerClosed {
			log.Fatalln("failed starting web on", srv.Addr, err)
		}
	}()

	for {
		<-c
		log.Println("terminate service")
		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 15*time.Second)
		defer cancel()

		log.Println("shutting down web on", srv.Addr)
		if err := srv.Shutdown(ctx); err != nil {
			log.Fatalln("failed shutdown server", err)
		}
		log.Println("web gracefully stopped")
		os.Exit(0)
	}
}
Copy
```

After that, run the Golang code with this command. 

```
go run main.goCopy
```

### 2.2 Verify Callback Request

In order to secure our resources from unauthenticated and unauthorized entities, it is crucial to verify that every event request to our bot server comes from SOP. To achieve that, we can check and validate the `signature` in the request header that will be sent by SOP for each callback API request.

Header

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Content-Type | string | Request header format |
| Signature | string | A signature to ensure that the request is sent by Seatalk |

```
package main

/* ... */

func WithSOPSignatureValidation() gin.HandlerFunc {
	return func(ctx *gin.Context) {
		r := ctx.Request
		signature := r.Header.Get("signature")

		if signature == "" {
			ctx.JSON(http.StatusForbidden, nil)
			return
		}

		body, err := io.ReadAll(r.Body)
		if err != nil {
			ctx.JSON(http.StatusInternalServerError, err.Error())
			return
		}

		hasher := sha256.New()
		signingSecret := "YOUR SIGNING SECRET" // Replace this with your Bot Signing Secret
		hasher.Write(append(body, []byte(signingSecret)...))
		targetSignature := hex.EncodeToString(hasher.Sum(nil))

		if signature != targetSignature {
			ctx.JSON(http.StatusForbidden, nil)
			return
		}

		r.Body = io.NopCloser(bytes.NewBuffer(body))
		ctx.Next()
	}
}

func main() {
	/* ... */
	r := gin.Default()
	r.Use(WithSOPSignatureValidation())
	/* ... */
}
Copy
```

To retrieve "YOUR SIGNING SECRET", you can see the Signing Secret value on Event Callback URL page (Step 2.4.5). Now our Bot will only receive request from SOP. Don't forget to re-run your code after applying the code above.

### 2.3 Handle Event: "event_verification" 

When configuring Callback URL (Step 2.4), to verify our Bot, SOP server will send a request to this endpoint. The request containing `seatalk_challenge` token and we need to send it again as the response. See this picture below to understand the flow. For complete documentation, can refer to this page Server API Event Callback (https://open.seatalk.io/docs/server-apis-event-callback).

![wGgmNT+S5L2mgAAAABJRU5ErkJggg==](data:image/png;base64,)

```
package main

/* ... */

type SOPEventCallbackReq struct {
	EventID string `json:"event_id"`
	EventType string `json:"event_type"`
	TimeStamp uint64 `json:"timestamp"`
	AppID string `json:"app_id"`
	Event Event `json:"event"`
}

type SOPEventVerificationResp struct {
	SeatalkChallenge string `json:"seatalk_challenge"`
}

type Event struct {
	SeatalkChallenge string `json:"seatalk_challenge"`
}

func main() {
	/* ... */
	r := gin.Default()
	r.Use(WithSOPSignatureValidation())

	r.POST("/callback", func(ctx *gin.Context) {
		var reqSOP SOPEventCallbackReq
		if err := ctx.BindJSON(&reqSOP); err != nil {
			ctx.JSON(http.StatusInternalServerError, "something wrong")
			return
		}
		log.Printf("INFO: received event with event_type %s", reqSOP.EventType)

		switch reqSOP.EventType {
		case "event_verification":
			ctx.JSON(http.StatusOK, SOPEventVerificationResp{SeatalkChallenge: reqSOP.Event.SeatalkChallenge})
		default:
			log.Printf("ERROR: event %s not handled yet!", reqSOP.EventType)
			ctx.JSON(http.StatusOK, "Success")
		}
	})
	/* ... */
}
Copy
```

Now our Bot can handle this event. Don't forget to re-run your code after applying the code above.

### 2.4 Configure Event Callback URL

To be able to receive event interaction, first you need to setup Bot Event Callback URL. Now, you can try to run the Golang program on your local computer. However, prior to this, you must expose your Localhost to the internet. You can use tools, something like ngrok (https://ngrok.com/). 

Ngrok, or other tools that suits you, works by forwarding your localhost address (127.0.0.1) and port (ex: 8080) to the internet. After installing the ngrok, you can run this command on your terminal

ngrok http 8080

The command above will launch the ngrok interface and there is a forwarding address, that is your server address and later this will be used to configure SOP Event Callback URL.

![tRCmNj7C5rYAAAAASUVORK5CYII=](data:image/png;base64,)

Assuming you have successfully configured the exposure of your local server to the internet, the next step is configuring the SOP Event Callback URL by following these steps. We'll using the "https://a215-103-86-128-2.ngrok-free.app" and append it with our endpoint "/callback", so it becomes "https://a215-103-86-128-2.ngrok-free.app/callback".

Step 2.4.1: Go to SeaTalk Open Platform's Developer Portal and enter the configuration page of the app that needs event callback capability.

Step 2.4.2: Click Event Callback on the left menu bar to enter the event callback configuration page.

![WQAAAAASUVORK5CYII=](data:image/png;base64,)

Step 2.4.3: Click the Edit icon beside the URL text box to enter the URL for verification.

![2Q==](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

Step 2.4.4: Fill the Event Callback URL, for example can use: `https://{{your_domain}}/callback` (e.g. `https://www.stockwatch.com/callback` )

Step 2.4.5: Click Save to trigger the callback URL verification test.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Step 2.4.6: Supported events will be automatically enabled for the bot after a callback URL is successfully configured.

Great! Now our Bot can be verified by SOP. Next, we will update our Bot, so that the Bot can receive event sent by SOP. To retrieve any event, that is an action that initiated by user, SOP will call our "/callback" API that we provide. Every Event have their own data schema, so in the next step we will give example with Event `message_from_bot_subscriber`. For list of complete Events, you can go to this docs https://open.seatalk.io/docs/list-of-events (https://open.seatalk.io/docs/list-of-events).

### 2.5 Handle Event: "message_from_bot_subscriber"

Note: We have removed the "subscriber" logic, but the related API names are retained for compatibility and continuity. Existing references to these endpoints remain valid, and users can now interact with the bot directly without the need to subscribe

When a user send message to the Bot, Bot will receive this event and later can construct response based on this message. In this example, we will just log or print the message we received, but later we will response every message with some template.

Event "message_from_bot_subscriber" have this parameter:

Header

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Content-Type | string | Request header format |
| Signature | string | A signature to ensure that the request is sent by SeaTalk |

Body

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| event_id | string | The ID of the event |
| event_type | string | The type of the event. It will be "message_from_bot_subscriber" in this case |
| timestamp | uint64 | The time when this event happened |
| app_id | string | The ID of the app to receive the event_notification |
| event | object | Event-specific information |
| ∟employee_code | string | The employee_code of the user |
| ∟message | object | The message received |

```
package main

/* ... */
type Event struct {
	SeatalkChallenge string `json:"seatalk_challenge"`
	EmployeeCode string `json:"employee_code"`
	Message Message `json:"message"`
}

type Message struct {
	Tag string `json:"tag"`
	Text TextMessage `json:"text"`
}

type TextMessage struct {
	Content string `json:"content"`
	PlainText string `json:"plain_text"`
}

func main() {
	/* ... */
	r := gin.Default()
	r.Use(WithSOPSignatureValidation())

	r.POST("/callback", func(ctx *gin.Context) {
		var reqSOP SOPEventCallbackReq
		if err := ctx.BindJSON(&reqSOP); err != nil {
			ctx.JSON(http.StatusInternalServerError, "something wrong")
			return
		}
		log.Printf("INFO: received event with event_type %s", reqSOP.EventType)

		switch reqSOP.EventType {
		case "event_verification":
			ctx.JSON(http.StatusOK, SOPEventVerificationResp{SeatalkChallenge: reqSOP.Event.SeatalkChallenge})
		case "message_from_bot_subscriber":
			// We'll use employee_code later to response user message
			log.Printf("INFO: message received: %s, with employee_code: %s", reqSOP.Event.Message.Text.Content, reqSOP.Event.EmployeeCode)
			ctx.JSON(http.StatusOK, "Success")
		default:
			log.Printf("ERROR: event %s not handled yet!", reqSOP.EventType)
			ctx.JSON(http.StatusOK, "Success")
		}
	})
	/* ... */
}Copy
```

Now our Bot able to receive message that sent by the bot user. Please try to send message to your newly created Bot, and make sure the log containing the message is there on your server. Don't forget to re-run your code after applying the code above.

![ASvtkanM2bOsAAAAAElFTkSuQmCC](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Now, we can see that when a user send a message, the Bot will log the message and the employee_code of the user (2...8). Later, this employee_code is needed when we want to initiate an action to the user, for example when Bot want to send a message to the user.

## 3. Initiate Action

### 3.1 Handle Authentication

In order to initiate an action by utilizing the SOP API, authentication of your Bot is necessary. To do that, we need to provide an `access_token` for every single request made to SOP API. This token can be obtained by calling the "Get Access Token" API and has a validity period of 7200 seconds. Please also keep in mind, that a caching mechanism is necessary to prevent procuring a new one for every request to SOP. For complete documentation, you can refer to this link Get App Access Token (https://open.seatalk.io/docs/get-app-access-token).

```
package main

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"log"
	"net/http"
	"time"

	"github.com/gin-gonic/gin"
)

type AppAccessToken struct {
	AccessToken string `json:"access_token"`
	ExpireTime uint64 `json:"expire"`
}

type SOPAuthAppResp struct {
	Code int `json:"code"`
	AppAccessToken string `json:"app_access_token"`
	Expire uint64 `json:"expire"`
}

var (
	appAccessToken AppAccessToken
)

func GetAppAccessToken() AppAccessToken {
	timeNow := time.Now().Unix()

	accTokenIsEmpty := appAccessToken == AppAccessToken{}
	accTokenIsExpired := appAccessToken.ExpireTime < uint64(timeNow)

	if accTokenIsEmpty || accTokenIsExpired {
		body := []byte(fmt.Sprintf(`{"app_id": "%s", "app_secret": "%s"}`, "<<YOUR APP ID>>", "<<YOUR APP SECRET>>"))

		req, err := http.NewRequest("POST", "https://openapi.seatalk.io/auth/app_access_token", bytes.NewBuffer(body))
		if err != nil {
			log.Printf("ERROR: [GetAppAccessToken] failed to create an HTTP request: %v", err)
			return appAccessToken
		}

		req.Header.Add("Content-Type", "application/json")

		client := &http.Client{}
		res, err := client.Do(req)
		if err != nil {
			log.Printf("ERROR: [GetAppAccessToken] failed to make an HTTP call to seatalk openapi.seatalk.io: %v", err)
			return appAccessToken
		}
		defer res.Body.Close()

		if res.StatusCode != 200 {
			log.Printf("ERROR: [GetAppAccessToken] got non 200 HTTP response status code: %v", err)
			return appAccessToken
		}

		resp := &SOPAuthAppResp{}
		if err := json.NewDecoder(res.Body).Decode(resp); err != nil {
			log.Printf("ERROR: [GetAppAccessToken] failed to parse response body: %v", err)
			return appAccessToken
		}

		if resp.Code != 0 {
			log.Printf("ERROR: [GetAppAccessToken] response code is not 0, error code %d, please refer to the error code documentation https://open.seatalk.io/docs/reference_server-api-error-code", resp.Code)
			return appAccessToken
		}

		appAccessToken = AppAccessToken{
			AccessToken: resp.AppAccessToken,
			ExpireTime: resp.Expire,
		}
	}

	return appAccessToken
}
Copy
```

![2Q==](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

To get your App ID and App Secret:

- Go to the SeaTalk Open Platform website and log in to your account.

- Click on the "Apps" tab.

- You can find the App ID and App Secret on the App's detail page. Click on the App name to access the detail page.

- Go to "Basic Info & Credentials" page, scroll down to "Credentials" section, and you can copy the App ID and App Secret

Now, your bot is authenticated to call SOP API!

### 3.2 Send Message to a Bot User

*Previously called "Send Message to a Bot Subscriber"

To sending a message to bot user, our Bot need to call SOP APIs. In this example, we will use API "Send Message to a Bot User". For complete list of API provided by SOP, you can go to this page https://open.seatalk.io/docs/Understanding-Bot-Capabilities (https://open.seatalk.io/docs/Understanding-Bot-Capabilities).

Now, "Send Message to a Bot User", have a request body structure like this.

Header

| Parameter | Type | Mandatory | Description | Default | Sample |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Authorization | string | Yes | Obtained through the Get App Access Token API | N/A | Bearer c8bda0f77ef940c5bea9f23b2d7fc0d8 |
| Content-Type | string | Yes | Request header format | N/A | application/json |

Body

| Parameter | Type | Mandatory | Description | Default | Length Limit | Sample |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| employee_code | string | Yes | The employee_code of the bot user | N/A | N/A | "e_12345678" |
| message | object | Yes | The message to be sent out | N/A | N/A | |

Message Object

| Parameter | Type | Mandatory | Description | Default | Length Limit | Sample |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| tag | string | Yes | The type of the message - be it "text" in this case | N/A | 20 characters | "text" |
| text | object | Yes | The text message object | N/A | N/A | |
| ∟format | int | No | The formatting to use in the content of the text message. Can be 1: Formatted text message (Markdown) 2: Plain text message | 1 | N/A | 1 |
| ∟content | string | Yes | - The content of the text message with markdown syntax supported - Refer to this document for supported markdown elements | N/A | Min: 1 character Max: 4096 characters | "How can I help you?" |

For the complete documentation of this event, you can read that here https://open.seatalk.io/docs/messaging_send-message-to-bot-user_ (https://open.seatalk.io/docs/messaging_send-message-to-bot-user_).

```
type SOPSendMessageToUser struct {
	EmployeeCode string `json:"employee_code"`
	Message SOPMessage `json:"message"`
}

type SOPMessage struct {
	Tag string `json:"tag"`
	Text SOPTextMsg `json:"text,omitempty"`
}

type SOPTextMsg struct {
	Format int8 `json:"format"`
	Content string `json:"content"`
}

type SendMessageToUserResp struct {
	Code int `json:"code"`
}

func SendMessageToUser(ctx context.Context, message, employeeCode string) error {
	bodyJson, _ := json.Marshal(SOPSendMessageToUser{
		EmployeeCode: employeeCode,
		Message: SOPMessage{
			Tag: "text",
			Text: SOPTextMsg{
				Format: 2, //plain text message
				Content: message,
			},
		},
	})

	req, err := http.NewRequest("POST", "https://openapi.seatalk.io/messaging/v2/single_chat", bytes.NewBuffer(bodyJson))
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}

	req.Header.Add("Content-Type", "application/json")

	// Every SOP API need an authorization, to make sure that our Bot is authorized to call that API. We will use the token that we retrieved on the Step 2.
	req.Header.Add("Authorization", "Bearer "+GetAppAccessToken().AccessToken)

	client := &http.Client{}
	res, err := client.Do(req)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer res.Body.Close()

	resp := &SendMessageToUserResp{}
	if err := json.NewDecoder(res.Body).Decode(resp); err != nil {
		return err
	}

	if resp.Code != 0 {
		return fmt.Errorf("something wrong, response code: %v", resp.Code)
	}

	return nil
}Copy
```

Now, we can send a message to our user! Next, it's time to combine all the previous code. Using the complete code, our Bot will response to every user message with "Hello World", by receiving event: "message_from_bot_subscriber" and calling API "Send Message to a Bot User". Don't forget that you can download the file with complete code by clicking this link (https://cdnid.sp-cdn.susercontent.com/api/v4/50093511/slimud/40d81634bea4a74147c260af616b2705/getting-started-bot.zip). 

Time to test our Bot! Now go to SeaTalk, search your Bot Name, and then send any message to the Bot. You should receive "Hello World" message.
